1.

By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the DAR filed by the investigating agency which has been converted into a claim petition under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of compensation to the petitioners who are Lrs of deceased victim namely Sh. Rahul, aged about MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 19 years 6 months in the road accident on 22.03.2021 at 3:00 pm, Near Holambi Mor, Alipur to Narela Road, Shahpur Garhi,
Delhi, involving vehicle i.e., TATA Ace bearing registration no. DL1PD-4467 (alleged offending vehicle) being driven in a rash and negligent manner by its driver (Respondent no.1 herein).
2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 22.03.2021, deceased Rahul was driving his vehicle i.e., TATA Ace bearing no. DL1L-AA-0156.

At about 3:00 PM, when he reached Near Holambi Mor, Alipur to Narela Road, Shahpur Garhi, Delhi, one TATA Ace bearing registration no. DL1PD-4467 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against the aforesaid vehicle of deceased, as a result of which, he sustained injuries.

Thereafter, deceased was immediately taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi,
where he was medically examined and ultimately, on 29.03.2021, he succumbed to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Postmortem on the body of deceased was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital, Delhi.

A case U/s 279/304A IPC was registered at PS. Narela Industrial Area vide FIR No.
133/21 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.

9.
For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW1 Vikas Kumar (IO of the case) is relevant.
He deposed in his evidence that he was the IO in this case.
He further deposed that he had filed the DAR and exhibited the same as Ex. PW2/1(colly).

10. Ld. counsel for insurance company vehemently argued that PW2 ASI Vikas Kumar is not an eye witness of the accident and no eye witness has been examined by petitioners during the course of inquiry.
He, therefore, contended that the petitioners have failed to prove that the accident in question was caused due to the negligent act of driver/R1.

On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for petitioners has heavily relied upon the criminal case record (which is part of DAR) in order to bring home his point that the accident in question had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

He further argued that respondent no. 1 Sh. Darshan was also chargesheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
12.

As already noted above, the respondent no. 3/insurance company has examined one witness i.e.,
R3W1 Sh. Darshan who is respondent no. 1/driver of offending vehicle in the present case in order to rebut the case of petitioners.
He deposed in his evidence that he was the respondent no. 1/driver in the present case.
He further deposed that on 22.03.2021, he had started his journey from Central Secretariat to Narela.
He further deposed that when he turned his vehicle at Holambi Mor and moved 500 meter ahead at a speed of 30-35 kmph, the driver of TATA Ace hit his bus.
He further deposed that the speed of TATA Ace was at about 70 kmph while the driver of TATA Ace was overtaking another TATA Ace and hit his bus from its front.
He further deposed that he was driving his vehicle at correct side at a very normal speed of 30-35 kmph and the accident was caused by the driver of TATA Ace by his sole and negligent driving.

He further deposed that he himself called the ambulance and he took the driver of TATA Ace namely MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS.
Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 Rahul to hospital in ambulance at Narela.
He deposed that no accident was caused by him as he was driving his vehicle at correct side and at very normal speed.
During his cross-examination on behalf of petitioners
, he admitted that FIR was registered by the police against him.
He further admitted that he was on bail.

He further admitted that police Vijay Kumar (Lrs Of Rahul) vs Darshan on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68113585/

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondents vehemently argued that the petitioners have failed to prove negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 in causing the accident.
For this purpose, they have heavily relied upon the testimony of R3W1 as discussed above.
On the other hand, Ld. counsel for petitioners argued that the testimony of R3W1 should not be believed as he is an interested witness.
He further submitted that FIR was registered against respondent no. 1 and he was on bail in the said case.
14. As regards the testimony of R3W1, it may be noted that he has simply deposed that deceased himself was solely negligent and responsible for the accident.
The respondent no. 1 has admitted during his cross- examination that FIR was registered by the police against him.
Thus, there is no reason to discard the testimony of PW2 made on oath.

15. Instead of referring to the series of decisions on the point in issue, it may be noted that it is well settled legal position as laid down by MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 Hon'ble Apex Court as well as by various High Courts in plethora of judgments delivered from time to time that in claim petitions preferred U/s 160/144 M.V Act, the claimants have to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of alleged offending vehicles by its drivers.
Same is the essence of legal position discussed by Hon'ble Apex Court in celebrated case of Meena Variyal mentioned supra.

At the same time, it is no more res-integra that claim petition filed under relevant provisions of M.V Act, is the outcome of social welfare legislation and the proceedings are summary in nature and do not require strict compliance of rules of evidence and pleadings.
It needs no emphasis that in case replies filed by respondents, are evasive then it is deemed that they have admitted the averments made by the claimants.

The purpose of granting compensation is to ameliorate the sufferings of the victims of Motor Vehicle Accidents and the niceties, hyper technicalities, procedural wrangles and tangles and mystic maybes have no role to play and same should not be any ground to dismiss the claim petitions and to defeat the rights of the claimants.

While saying so, I am fortified by the decisions rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases titled as " N.KV. Bros (P) Ltd Vs. M. Karumai Ammal", 1980 ACJ 435 (SC); " Sohan Lal Passi Vs. P. Sesh Reddy", 1996 ACJ 1044 (SC) and "
Dulcina Fernandes Vs. Joaquim Xavier Cruz", 2013 ACJ 2712 (SC).

In the above cited decision, the claimants had not examined any eyewitness.

Still, Hon'ble Apex Court held that in view of filing of criminal case record including charge-sheet showing that driver of alleged offending vehicle had been charge-sheeted for causing the accident due to rash and negligent driving of said vehicle and the driver himself did not enter into witness box, claimants were able to prove the issue of accident being caused due to rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by said driver on the basis of pre-ponderance of the probabilities.
MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 18.
Now, turning back to the facts of the present case.

No doubt, the petitioners have not examined any eye witness to prove the negligence on the part of driver of the alleged vehicle described above but nevertheless, there is ample material brought on record during the course of inquiry, which is sufficient to establish that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver/Respondent no. 1.
19.
It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 133/21 u/s 279/304A IPC was registered at PS. Narela Industrial Area with regard to accident in question.

Copy of chargesheet filed in criminal case (which is part of DAR) would show that Sh. Darshan (Respondent no.1) has been chargesheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC by Investigating Agency after arriving at the conclusion that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Same would also point out that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by respondent no. 1.
20.

Not only this, copy of PM Report (which is also part of DAR) of deceased, would show that his cause of death was cranio-cerebral damage and multiple injuries sustained as a result of blunt force impact to the head.
All the injuries were ante-mortem in nature and could be possible in the manner a alleged.

The injuries as noted in the relevant column with regard to external injuries, as mentioned therein, are consistent with the injuries which MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the aforesaid document from the side of respondents.

21. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that deceased Rahul had sustained fatal injuries in the road accident which took place on 22.03.2021 at 3:00 pm,
Near Holambi Mor, Alipur to Narela Road, Shahpur Garhi, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no. 1/driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, this issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.

sentences.text:
The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' MACP No. 309/21; FIR No.
133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
23. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

Ld. Counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that since deceased was not having permanent job and he was aged about 20 years at the time of accident, future prospects @ 40% should also be awarded in favour of the petitioners.

29. As already noted above, PW1 Sh. Vijay Kumar, who is father of deceased deposed in his evidence that deceased was the owner-cum-driver of Tata Ace vehicle and was earning Rs. 35,000/- per month at the time of accident.

Apart from the bald statement made by PW1 that deceased was earning Rs. 35,000/- per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove the monthly income of deceased at the time of accident in question.
However, petitioners have filed School Leaving Certificate (Ex. PW1/8) of deceased in proof of educational qualification document of the deceased.
30. It is seen that the petitioners are not having any proof regarding income of deceased.

However,
the petitioners have relied upon copy of 10 th class marksheet of deceased.
As per the said document, deceased was 10 th class pass at the time of accident.

Thus, in the absence of any relevant document in respect of working and earning of deceased, I am of the view MACP No. 309/21; FIR No. 133/21; PS. Narela Industrial Area DOD:07.03.2026 that income of deceased should be assessed as per the minimum wages of a Matriculate person, applicable in the State of Delhi as on the date of accident.

The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were revised to Rs. 19,291/- w.e.f.
01.04.2021.
The accident in question had occurred on 22.03.2021 i.e., just 9 days before the date from which minimum wages were revised by the government.
In these facts and circumstances, I am inclined to take the minimum wages at the rate of Rs. 19,291/-in order to calculate loss of dependency.
(Reliance placed on unreported decision in the matter titled as "THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO.LTD. Vs. CHHOTEY LAL & ORS. ", in MAC. APP. 1074/2016 decided on 15.05.2017 by Hon'ble Delhi High Court).
